A student came to Eric Cogorno struggling with weak right shots and poor contact — a pattern that had been holding him back for years — and made huge gains in 15 to 20 minutes from one micro move. The fix is the trail elbow pit pointing away from the body while the elbow works forward, combined with independent forearm rotation to square the club face at impact. Watch how Adam Scott and Tommy Fleetwood keep the elbow pit away throughout the entire downswing while forearm rotation delivers a square club face — and how the plate drill and ping pong paddle drill give any golfer the same feel immediately. These golf tips for beginners and improving golfers produce better golf swing consistency, solid contact, and a fix for the weak right miss that most golfers struggle with for years. If you leave this video without trying the plate drill, you’re leaving golf swing consistency and solid contact on the table.

What You’ll Learn:
• Why the trail elbow pit must point away from the body as the elbow works forward — and what happens when it rotates toward the target instead
• How independent forearm rotation squares the club face while keeping the elbow pit away — the micro move that fixes weak right shots
• Why keeping the elbow pit away prevents early release and produces correct shaft lean at impact
• How Adam Scott demonstrates the elbow pit staying away and forearm rotation delivering a square club face through impact
• How Tommy Fleetwood uses the same elbow pit away position regardless of grip strength — and why every golfer needs some version of this move
• The plate drill for training elbow pit away and forearm rotation without a club — the starting point Eric used with his student
• The ping pong paddle drill for feeling correct forearm rotation with the shoulder staying down through impact
• How to use ball flight as feedback — right miss means more rotation, left miss means less — for better golf swing consistency

videos.summary_source_text:
NEW SQ9 is the BIGGEST Audi EVER! Is the new Audi Q9 more luxurious than an A8?! 

Get 20% off CarVertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

Mat’s flown over to Utah to get his hands on the Audi SQ9! 

It’s the first generation of the Audi Q9 & SQ9, and it sits right at the top of the Audi range. What’s more, it’s also the largest Audi ever produced! 

So with that in mind, should you choose it over class-leading 7-seaters like the BMW X7 and Mercedes GLS? Let’s take a closer look, starting with the design… 

From the outside, there’s no denying the all-new Q9 is a super large & imposing beast. Up front, there are similarities between the entry-level Q9 and this SQ9, although the latter has a more aggressive look to it, thanks to a different bumper and grille design. The large grille is flanked on either side by Audi’s class-leading DRLs, and the main headlights sit in a separate unit on the front end. Around the side, the SQ9 is given more definition thanks to chrome surrounds on the windows, chrome roof rails and creases along the doors. At the back, Audi has fitted the SQ9 with 100% real quad tailpipes, as well as wraparound OLED taillights!

On the inside, the SQ9 looks largely similar to all other recent Audis - but that’s no bad thing! The dashboard comes absolutely covered in screens, with the wraparound digital dial and infotainment screen, coupled with a passenger screen. There are little to no physical buttons, so everything is controlled through the screen. The materials are nice throughout the entire cabin, and the seats are large and comfortable. 

In the back, the SQ9 is available in a 6- or 7-seat configuration. The car we have here has the six seats, and the captain’s chairs are large, comfortable, and come with a high amount of movement. Simply put, the SQ9 is cavernous for passengers in the back! 

The Q9 series is available with a choice of either a V6 petrol or diesel, and a plug-in hybrid will also be available. However, in the range-topping SQ9 you’ll find a 4-litre twin-turbo V8 under the bonnet, and this delivers a huge 600hp and 800Nm of torque! 

As for price, the Q9 range starts from £103,900, rising to around £130,000 for this SQ9. But does it offer enough to sway you away from BMW or Mercedes? Let us know which you’d choose in the comments!

videos.title: 26.10.26 - Ep.26 (Part 2) - Execution, Market Makers & The True Cost of Liquidity
videos.summary_source_text:
26.10.26 - Ep.26 (Part 2) - Execution, Market Makers & The True Cost of Liquidity The price you see on a chart is not necessarily the price you receive. In Episode 26 Part 2, we explore execution, the hidden costs of trading, and the role market makers play in connecting buyers and sellers.

We also begin the transition from market understanding to practical prop-trading preparation: execute with awareness, measure risk, and review each decision.

THE LAST PRICE IS NOT YOUR PRICE

Charts show past transactions. Your order interacts with the market now, and its fill depends on the current bid and ask, depth, order queue, volatility, trade size, latency and competing orders.

Large orders may fill across several price levels. Even correct analysis can lose its edge through poor execution: being right about direction is not the same as trading well.

EXECUTION IS PART OF RISK MANAGEMENT

Risk begins with the order. Spreads, slippage, partial fills, market impact and limited exit liquidity can all change a trade's outcome.

The full cost of execution may include:
• Explicit trading fees
• The bid-ask spread
• Slippage
• Market impact
• Opportunity cost when an order never fills

For example, if you intend to deploy $100,000 and execution works against you by 20 basis points (0.20%), that difference equals $200. At 50 basis points, it equals $500. Repeated across trades, these costs matter.

PROP-TRADING READINESS: STAGE ONE

Professional trading means reviewing execution, not just profit and loss. Stage One is execution awareness: record how well you followed your process.

For every practice trade, record:
• Decision price
• Best bid and best ask
• Bid-ask spread
• Order type
• Intended entry and actual fill
• Slippage and position size
• Market conditions and exit type
• Execution notes

Use screenshots or screen recordings to review each order. Complete a daily execution sheet consistently. Ask: “Did I execute the plan correctly?” A winning trade can be poorly executed, while a losing trade can still reflect a disciplined process.

You do not need to trade faster, use more leverage or add ten new indicators. Observe carefully and understand the chain from decision, to order, to fill, to position, to exit. While practising, keep leverage low and focus on consistency rather than chasing profits.

Before every practice trade, ask:
• What size am I asking the market to fill, and at what price?
• What spread am I paying?
• How much liquidity is available?
• Which order type am I using?
• What happens if liquidity disappears before I exit?

Reviewing your records can help assess consistency and strategy performance. This is preparation for prop trading, not a promise of passing a challenge or making profits.

WHO PROVIDES LIQUIDITY?

Market makers stand between buyers and sellers by quoting prices at which they are willing to buy and sell. They help match buyers and sellers when natural counterparties are not immediately available.

For example, a market maker might quote a bid of $99.98 and an ask of $100.02. The difference is the spread. But market making is not simply buying low, selling high and collecting easy money. When a market maker buys an asset, it holds inventory and remains exposed to price movements until it can sell or hedge that position.

If a market maker buys 10,000 shares at $99.98 and the price falls to $99.50, the $0.48 move represents a $4,800 decline in the value of that inventory. Spread revenue is only one part of the economics; inventory risk, hedging, funding and fees also matter.

ADVERSE SELECTION & WIDENING SPREADS

Adverse selection is the risk of trading with someone whose information or reaction is better or faster. When prices rapidly re-adjust, a quote can become stale and expose the market maker to an unfavourable move.

This helps explain why spreads can widen during uncertainty. Before major economic news, volatility and hedging costs can rise. Market makers may respond with a lower bid and higher ask to compensate for added risk.

Liquidity is not fixed. It can become more expensive precisely when market participants most urgently need to trade.

THE PROFESSIONAL SHIFT

Episode 25 explored how capital moves. Episode 26 asks how the market absorbs that movement through liquidity, order books, spreads, execution and the participants willing to take the other side of a trade.

Questions evolve from “What is the price?” to “How much liquidity is available around that price?” From “I pressed Buy at $100” to “Where did my order actually fill?” And from “Was I right about direction?” to “Was my execution efficient, and did I follow my process?”

Next, we continue with market-maker inventory and how liquidity providers manage their exposure.

videos.title: Hindi - 26.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 26.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

videos.title: What Do the Avalanche Need to Change After the Recent Stretch of Subpar Play?
videos.summary_source_text:
What Do the Avalanche Need to Change After the Recent Stretch of Subpar Play? Colorado Avalanche fans question the team’s urgency as a frustrating performance streak raises alarms. With star Gabriel Landeskog bluntly stating “we sucked,” is it time for coach Jared Bednar to shake up the lines or stay patient? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the Avalanche’s recent lack of execution, missed puck battles, and overreliance on talent, sparking debate about whether small adjustments or bigger changes are needed.

Key topics include Nathan MacKinnon’s role, social media overreactions, and whether shot quantity could reignite the offense. Listeners weigh in on the team’s mindset, the search for “greasy” goals over pretty plays, and the importance of consistent speed. Closing with analysis of Connor Hellebuyck’s trade to the New Jersey Devils and its impact on the Western Conference, the show offers critical insights into what’s next for the Avalanche in a pivotal moment of the NHL season.

videos.title: The Real Cause of Tinnitus (It's Not in Your Ears)
videos.summary_source_text:
The Real Cause of Tinnitus (It's Not in Your Ears) Tinnitus, or ringing in the ears, involves more than just the ears themselves. The brain stem plays an important role in how these phantom sounds are perceived, especially when the inner ear isn’t receiving enough energy to function properly.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/LZNf7O4fqSc 

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/47Act5U

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

When energy levels in the inner ear drop, the brain stem compensates by increasing its sensitivity to sound. GABA, a neurotransmitter that helps calm nerve activity, normally helps regulate this response.

Vitamin B1 is important for both energy production in the inner ear and GABA function. A deficiency can interfere with these processes and contribute to tinnitus symptoms.

Allithiamine is a form of vitamin B1 originally derived from garlic that can cross the blood-brain barrier and help support energy production and GABA activity in the brainstem.

videos.summary_source_text:
7 Daily Habits That Are Making Your Brain Age Faster | Dr. Mandell Are your everyday habits silently aging your brain faster than they should? Memory loss, brain fog, poor concentration, and cognitive decline may be influenced by daily choices you don't even realize you're making. In this powerful video, Dr. Alan Mandell reveals 7 everyday habits that could be affecting your brain health, including sitting too long, poor sleep, elevated blood sugar, high blood pressure, untreated hearing loss, air pollution, and lack of mental stimulation. A small change in your grip may help make this chest exercise more comfortable without completely changing the way you press. In this video, I show you a dumbbell bench press tip that shifts the focus from how much weight you can lift to how your wrists feel while you lift it.

Train Smarter Here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe to This Channel Here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

First, look at your current dumbbell bench press form. Watch the clips in this video and compare them to how you hold your dumbbells, especially at the top of each rep. Are you forcing both ends of the dumbbell to stay perfectly level with the floor? Or do you allow a slight tilt, with your thumb sitting a little higher than your pinky?

The goal here is to find a comfortable, controlled grip that lets you train your chest without your wrists becoming the limiting factor. If every set is interrupted by wrist discomfort, adding more weight is not the answer. Before you worry about progressing your dumbbell bench press, pay attention to where the handle sits in your hand and whether your wrist position changes as you press.

The adjustment shown starts with moving your hand slightly toward the thumb side of the dumbbell handle. Instead of insisting that the dumbbell remain perfectly horizontal, allow the pinky side to sit slightly lower. Watch the demonstration closely. This is a small adjustment in how you hold and balance the weight, not a cue to force your wrist into an exaggerated angle.

Why might this help? The position of the dumbbell in your hand changes how the load is supported at your wrist. A grip that looks symmetrical does not automatically feel comfortable for every person. The video explains the wrist positioning using the radius and ulna, the two bones of the forearm. The practical takeaway is to evaluate whether a subtle change in grip reduces the pinching or pressure you notice during the exercise.

That does not mean every case of wrist pain comes from the same problem, or that one grip adjustment will fix every painful wrist. It means your dumbbell grip is worth checking. Use a light pair of dumbbells to compare the positions shown so that you can focus on control and comfort.

There is another detail to pay attention to: how you squeeze the handle. In the demonstration, the emphasis shifts toward the thumb and index finger. Keep the remaining fingers wrapped securely around the dumbbell for stability. This is not a reason to loosen your hand or let the dumbbell move around during the set.

Think of this as a cue to make your grip more deliberate. Rather than simply grabbing the dumbbells and starting your reps, take a moment to establish the position before you press. Notice where the handle rests, how the dumbbell balances and whether you can maintain that setup throughout the movement. Your grip should feel secure at the bottom, through the press and at the top.

Keep the purpose of the adjustment in mind. We are trying to make the dumbbell bench press more comfortable for your wrists so you can focus on training your chest. You do not need to turn this into a test of how much more weight you can lift. If the lighter dumbbells feel better, practice the setup and make sure the same comfort and control carry over from rep to rep.

Also, do not confuse the slight tilt shown here with allowing the weight to fold your wrist backward. Pay attention to the full demonstration rather than copying only the appearance of the dumbbells at lockout. A useful technique change is one you can control throughout the set, without creating a new uncomfortable position elsewhere.

If you have been searching for how to stop wrist pain during dumbbell bench press, start by watching your grip as closely as you watch your pressing technique. This small detail may be the adjustment that helps you perform the exercise more comfortably. If the change hurts, stop. Persistent or worsening wrist pain deserves an assessment rather than repeated attempts to push through it.

Try the grip adjustment shown in your next chest workout with a light weight and see how your wrists respond. The priority is a secure grip, controlled reps and a chest exercise that feels comfortable.

If you want to apply this tip to a complete workout program, be sure to visit athleanx.com and use the program selector tool to find the program that matches your current goals. By training like an athlete you can see some of your fastest increases in strength and muscle size over the next 90 days.

For more videos on how to fix your aches and pains, especially in the gym, then be sure to subscribe to our channel here on youtube and remember to turn on your notifications so you never miss a new video when it’s published. videos.title: Gemini 5 Is Here: Google’s 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 5 Is Here: Google’s 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade! Google's next AI model may already be hiding in plain sight. A leaked internal codename, Carbon, is fueling speculation about Gemini 5, with one Google employee reportedly comparing its coding abilities to Claude Opus 5.5. But there's no benchmark, no official announcement, and no confirmed release date.

Meanwhile, Google's newly released Gemini 4 Argon is already producing some remarkable results: outperforming GPT-6 Astra by roughly 12 points on a long-context benchmark, working autonomously for 11 hours inside a 205,000-line codebase, and powering AI agents that defeated Minecraft's Ender Dragon after 27 hours and 605 deaths.

So what exactly is Google building with Carbon? And could the next Gemini model challenge OpenAI and Anthropic where it matters most?

The story starts with an October 9 Business Insider report revealing three internal Google codenames: Argon, Barium, and Carbon. While speculation has connected Carbon to Gemini 5, the report describes it as a new version of Gemini 4. And Barium-B reportedly became the checkpoint Google selected for Argon.

That distinction changes how we should interpret the leak.

Gemini 4 Argon launched with a roughly one-million-token shared context window, three thinking levels, and introductory API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Google also introduced long-running background tasks and continuation-based generation.

But the more interesting story is what Argon can accomplish when connected to external tools.

Argon proposed six performance optimizations across 32 files. Human maintainers rejected four, but two shipped, reducing session-preparation overhead by approximately 40% in long sessions and improving package import performance by roughly 21%.

That's impressive, but it also reveals something important about autonomous AI agents: generating improvements and producing reliable, production-ready code are not the same thing.

Then there's Minecraft.

Four Gemini 4 Argon agents collaborated for 27 hours and 14 minutes, writing 2,783 programs, exchanging 229 messages, and dying 605 times before defeating the Ender Dragon. The experiment demonstrates long-term agent persistence, but it also depended on external memory, coordination systems, and the Mineflayer framework.

The benchmark picture is equally complicated.

On Google's published evaluations, Argon beat GPT-6 Astra on GraphWalks with 84.2 versus 71.8. It also posted strong results on LABBench 2 and the Vals Index.

But coding benchmarks tell a different story.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Claude Opus 5.5 scored 66.4 against Argon's 57.4. On FrontierSWE v2, GPT-6 Astra reached 65.5 while Argon managed 55.0.

Google's AI leadership looks very different depending on what you're measuring.

Beyond coding, Google is making ambitious claims about scientific discovery, quantum computing, molecular modeling, robotics, and fusion research.

We examine reported improvements to xTB molecular modeling, a quantum circuit with dramatically reduced spacetime cost, AI-designed enzymes, and a rare-disease genomic analysis.

We also look at Gemini Robotics 2, Boston Dynamics' Spot, simulation-generated robot training, and a reported improvement in real-world robotic task success from 56% to 75%.

But these results come with important qualifications. Some involve publicly inspectable code. Others rely on internal Google evaluations, limited experiments, or research that still requires independent replication.

And that's what makes Carbon so interesting.

If Argon already demonstrates this level of long-context reasoning, autonomous coding, tool orchestration, and scientific assistance, what could Google's next internal checkpoint deliver?

Could Carbon close the gap with Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents? Could it improve long-running autonomous workflows? And is Google preparing another Gemini 4 model rather than the Gemini 5 release everyone expects?

We separate confirmed releases from leaked information, published benchmarks from company claims, and genuine technical progress from the speculation surrounding Google's next AI model.

Subscribe to BitBiased for detailed coverage of Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, AI agents, emerging technology, and the competition shaping the next generation of artificial intelligence.

videos.title: The Truth About Wedge Bounce: Don’t Buy Wedges Until You Watch This
videos.summary_source_text:
The Truth About Wedge Bounce: Don’t Buy Wedges Until You Watch This Ever wondered: what is wedge bounce, what does bounce on wedges do, and how does it actually impact your chipping? In this video, we break down wedge bounce explained simply—debunking common short game myths and revealing how sole grind and vertical face strike dictate your launch, spin, and scoring.

Most golfers are told that high bounce is for diggers and low bounce is for sweepers, but bounce is completely dynamic. Watch to see how bounce acts as an "insurance policy" through the turf, why sole relief and grind let you open the face cleanly, and how choosing the right sole setup stops thinned chips on hardpan or dead, floating shots out of fluffy grass.

videos.summary_source_text:
Every shot from WEATHER DELAY 3-hole playoff | Butterfield Bermuda Championship | 2026 Due to the unfavorable weather forecast at the 2026 Butterfield Bermuda Championship, Saturday's tournament results were considered final through 54 holes in accordance with PGA Tour Regulations. A playoff between Seamus Power and Austin Smotherman took place Monday, October 26th to determine the champion.

The Butterfield Bermuda Championship returns to Port Royal Golf Course as the FedExCup Fall continues, with defending champion Adam Schenk looking to make history by becoming the event’s first successful title defender. Austin Smotherman arrives fresh off his maiden PGA TOUR victory, while in-form Ben James boasts three consecutive top five finishes. Corey Conners headlines the field by world ranking, with rising stars Miles Russell, Neal Shipley and Mason Howell also teeing it up. Thiamine, or vitamin B1, is essential for maintaining healthy nerves and supporting normal brain function.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/8OSlBn6qRqs

Signs and symptoms of vitamin B1 deficiency include:
• Nerve pain, including sciatica
• Tremors
• Anxiety and feelings of impending doom
• Difficulty focusing and concentrating
• Racing thoughts and insomnia
• Restless legs and lactic acid buildup
• Air hunger and poor exercise tolerance
• Burning feet, numbness, and tingling associated with peripheral neuropathy

Vitamin B1 also plays an important role in maintaining the protective myelin coating around nerves. When B1 is deficient, nerve function can be disrupted and contribute to burning, tingling, and other unusual sensations in the feet or hands.

videos.title: A DRAMATIC and TENSE Sunday Finish | 2026 Genesis Championship
videos.summary_source_text:
A DRAMATIC and TENSE Sunday Finish | 2026 Genesis Championship Watch the Back Nine on Sunday, presented by Nexo, as Yuto Katsuragawa’s patience pays off with a two-shot victory at the 2026 Genesis Championship, earning him his second DP World Tour title.

Katsuragawa began the week 106th in the Race to Dubai Rankings. The win lifts him into the top 70 and secures his place in the DP World Tour Play-Offs.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 38 events, the immediate future for some players on the DP World Tour depends on their performance at this week's Genesis Championship, the final event of the regular season brings drama aplenty and for the third year running South Korea is the base for it to unfold. Following on from Byeong Hun An's success two years ago, it was Junghwan Lee who triumphed 12 months ago as he became a DP World Tour winner for the first time. There are 39 players from South Korea teeing it up, headlined by recent Presidents Cup teammates Si Woo Kim and Sungjae Im as they look add DP World Tour glory to their CVs. Eugenio Chacarra will aim to bolster his lead at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World, following a run of form that has seen him finish third, second and then first last week in India across his last three starts. He is one of 11 winners from this season on the DP World Tour teeing up, with fellow multiple winner Casey Jarvis and Open champion Ryan Fox among them. The leading 70 available players in the Rankings at the end of this week will play their way into the field for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship next month. The top 50 after that will earn a place at the DP World Tour Championship, the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events.

videos.title: The Road Struggles Continue For the Avalanche In An Ugly Loss to the Nashville Predators
videos.summary_source_text:
The Road Struggles Continue For the Avalanche In An Ugly Loss to the Nashville Predators Colorado Avalanche stumble to a 6-2 defeat against the Nashville Predators, raising urgent questions about their road game woes and special teams collapse. Despite Devon Toews finding the net, the Avalanche looked lethargic and uninspired, outshot and outplayed by a Nashville team coming off a back-to-back. Can Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar spark a turnaround before these struggles become a season-long trend?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down a night filled with costly penalties, ineffective power plays, and defensive miscues that left Scott Wedgewood exposed. The conversation explores concerns around the team’s shot selection, neutral zone turnovers, and lack of support from depth forwards. Listeners get key stats, heat map analysis, and spirited fan reactions as the hosts debate whether this ugly loss could serve as a necessary wake-up call for Jared Bednar’s squad. Will the Avalanche find consistency before November?

videos.title: Inconsistency? Change what your hands are doing
videos.summary_source_text:
Inconsistency? Change what your hands are doing If you’re struggling with inconsistent ball striking, chunks, thin shots, or a golf swing that feels all arms, look down before you start changing what your hands are doing. 👀⛳️

Your pressure shift might be the missing piece.
Watch the feet and hips closely in this video, because the important part isn’t just where your weight goes, it’s when it gets there.

In the backswing, pressure loads into the trail side, staying more toward the inside of the trail foot rather than drifting to the outside.

But here’s the part a lot of golfers miss:
You don’t wait until the backswing is finished to start moving toward the target.
As the club is finishing the backswing, pressure is already beginning to move toward the lead side.

That gives you a better opportunity to rotate through the shot instead of:
→ Hanging back on your trail foot
→ Sliding through impact
→ Throwing the arms at the ball
→ Trying to save the strike at the last second

Think of the sequence as:
LOAD → SHIFT → ROTATE

Not:
LOAD → WAIT → PANIC. 😅

And this is why simply watching weight-shift videos can only get you so far.
You may understand exactly what you’re supposed to do and still have no idea whether you’re actually doing it.

That’s the problem the Ball First Board is designed to solve.

videos.summary_source_text:
Paul Maurice, Panthers Postgame: Florida Ends Two-Game Slide, Beat Chicago Blackhawks Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice speaks to the media in Chicago after his team beat the Blackhawks 3-2 on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026.

Florida was coming off a 4-0 to the Penguins on Thursday and had lost two straight after losing 5-1 in Ottawa on Wednesday. 

Down 1-0 early Sunday, Sandis Vilmanis scored his first of the season before Matthew Tkachuk scored off a Seth Jones shot. 

Tied late, Lars Eller got his first with the Panthers with 2:23 left for the win. 

The Panthers end this road trip with the first of a home-and-home with the Winnipeg Jets. Florida is in Winnipeg on Tuesday; the Jets visit Sunrise on Friday.

videos.title: Elon Musk's Grok 5: A 6 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
Elon Musk's Grok 5: A 6 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade! Elon Musk says Grok 5 will have **6 trillion parameters**, native multimodal intelligence, real-time video understanding, and a 10% chance of achieving AGI. But Grok 5 has already missed multiple release windows, xAI hasn't published its official specifications, and the latest Grok 4.7 benchmarks reveal a much more complicated story.

So how close is xAI to delivering the AI model Musk has been promising?

In January 2026, xAI officially confirmed that Grok 5 was training. Musk later connected that training to Colossus 2, part of xAI's massive AI infrastructure expansion. But despite claims about a six-trillion-parameter model, dynamic reinforcement learning, autonomous tool creation, and human-level AI capabilities, there is still no published Grok 5 model card, verified architecture, API pricing, or independent benchmark result.

And the release timeline keeps shifting.

Musk initially suggested Grok 5 would arrive before the end of 2025. That moved to Q1 2026, then to a less specific roadmap involving Grok 4.7, Grok 4.8, and Grok 4.9. By September 2026, even Musk's predictions about Grok 5 outperforming everything had become more cautious.

Meanwhile, **Grok 4.7 is giving us the clearest evidence of what xAI can actually deliver.**

Released September 21, 2026, Grok 4.7 introduced a larger base model, extended reinforcement learning, improved self-verification, and deeper integration with the Grok Bot agent harness. Its 500,000-token context window and focus on long-running coding tasks reveal where xAI is concentrating its development.

The benchmark improvements are significant:

- Terminal-Bench 4.0: 20.3% → 37.6%
- EEBench: 53.0% → 64.0%
- CursorBench 4.0: 40.4% → 46.3%
- Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index: 56, up 9 points

But there's an important catch. Grok 4.7 was often tested at higher reasoning effort than Grok 4.6, consuming substantially more output tokens. Its broader Intelligence Index improved by only about two points, while some long-context and automation benchmarks actually declined.

And compared with competitors like **GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Gemini 4 Argon**, Grok 4.7 still trails the frontier in several important areas.

Pricing adds another dimension. Grok 4.7 starts at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, making it competitive on paper. But higher reasoning-token consumption, premium pricing for Grok 4.7 Fast, and expensive long-running agent workflows complicate the real cost comparison.

We also examine xAI's Grok Build demonstrations, independent agent testing, hallucination measurements, and the company's reported safety improvements. Then there's Colossus: more than one million H100 GPU equivalents across xAI's infrastructure, but no disclosed figure showing how much compute Grok 5 itself is actually using.

Does enormous computing power guarantee a breakthrough? Does a six-trillion-parameter claim tell us anything meaningful without knowing the architecture? And what evidence would Grok 5 need to establish itself as the world's leading AI model?

This is a detailed breakdown of **Grok 5's release delays, Elon Musk's AGI predictions, Grok 4.7's actual performance, the competition, and the evidence still missing from xAI's biggest promises.**

Discover what causes this condition, how to fix a Dowager’s hump, and the best thoracic spine exercises for posture correction.

👉 Download Dr. Berg’s Free Daily Health Routine: https://drbrg.co/4zi73Za

Your neck hump or upper back hump may not be caused by what you think. Press on the hump. Is it soft and spongy like a fat pad or hard, firm, and rigid? This can help determine the underlying cause and the best way to address it.

A Dowager’s hump can be a postural or structural issue. Postural problems can often be corrected with the right stretches and exercises. A structural Dowager’s hump involves wedged vertebrae, often caused by osteoporosis, and requires an X-ray for diagnosis.

A buffalo hump is different. It involves a fat pad at the base of the neck and is often associated with elevated cortisol, insulin resistance, and Cushing's syndrome.

If your neck hump is associated with osteoporosis, focus on calcium, collagen, trace minerals, magnesium, vitamin D3, vitamin K2, and weight training to support stronger bones.

If you’re dealing with a buffalo hump caused by a fat pad, check your fasting insulin levels. A high-carb diet and frequent eating may contribute to insulin resistance. A low-carb diet and intermittent fasting may help address the underlying metabolic problem.

videos.title: What Happens If You Take Potassium Every Day?
videos.summary_source_text:
What Happens If You Take Potassium Every Day? Your body needs approximately 4700 mg of potassium every day, yet most people don’t even get half that amount. Potassium is essential for producing the electrical activity that keeps your cells functioning, your muscles contracting, and your heart beating.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/1hXpb3T96PU

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4el6vJG

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

Potassium works with sodium to power the sodium-potassium pumps in your cells. These tiny pumps act like batteries, generating the electrical impulses your body needs for energy, muscle function, and a normal heartbeat.

Signs of low potassium can include:

• Fatigue and low energy
• Muscle cramps
• Heart palpitations
• High blood pressure

Some of the best potassium-rich foods include avocados, leafy greens, and salmon.

videos.summary_source_text:
Round 4 Highlights | 2026 Genesis Championship Final round highlights of the 2026 Genesis Championship featuring Casey Jarvis, Ryan Fox, Si Woo Kim, Martin Couvra and Yuto Katsuragawa.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 38 events, the immediate future for some players on the DP World Tour depends on their performance at this week's Genesis Championship, the final event of the regular season brings drama aplenty and for the third year running South Korea is the base for it to unfold. Following on from Byeong Hun An's success two years ago, it was Junghwan Lee who triumphed 12 months ago as he became a DP World Tour winner for the first time. There are 39 players from South Korea teeing it up, headlined by recent Presidents Cup teammates Si Woo Kim and Sungjae Im as they look add DP World Tour glory to their CVs. Eugenio Chacarra will aim to bolster his lead at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World, following a run of form that has seen him finish third, second and then first last week in India across his last three starts. He is one of 11 winners from this season on the DP World Tour teeing up, with fellow multiple winner Casey Jarvis and Open champion Ryan Fox among them. The leading 70 available players in the Rankings at the end of this week will play their way into the field for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship next month. The top 50 after that will earn a place at the DP World Tour Championship, the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events.

Welcome to the Official YouTube channel of the DP World Tour. Every week you can find extended tournament highlights and individual player highlights from the likes of Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood. What Happens to Your Body Years After Gallbladder Removal? Years after gallbladder removal, changes in bile flow can affect how well you digest fats and absorb fat-soluble vitamins. The gallbladder normally stores and concentrates bile, then releases it when you eat. Without it, bile continuously trickles into the small intestine instead.

Over time, this can affect the absorption of:
• Vitamin A
• Vitamin D
• Vitamin E
• Vitamin K1
• Vitamin K2

Low levels of these nutrients can contribute to issues like dry eyes, night vision problems, achy bones, changes in mood, easy bruising, and calcium buildup in soft tissues.

Ox bile can be taken after meals to support fat digestion, while TUDCA is another bile salt that can be taken on an empty stomach when needed.

videos.title: Claude Duet Is Here: Anthropic's AI Agent That Works While You're Away
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Duet Is Here: Anthropic's AI Agent That Works While You're Away Anthropic says Claude Duet supports over 6,000 connectors and plugins. But its public Marketplace shows only about 1,350, Microsoft 365 isn't supported in Duet, and the AI that's supposed to work proactively only checks your accounts every few hours. So how much of Anthropic's new AI agent is actually working, and how much is still a promise?

Launched October 21, Claude Duet is Anthropic's new proactive AI agent powered by Claude Opus 5.5. Unlike a traditional chatbot, Duet can contact you first, monitor connected accounts, prepare morning briefings, follow up on forgotten conversations, and complete delegated tasks using its own cloud computer—even after you close the app.

But there's a catch: every background check consumes your existing Claude usage allowance.

Claude Duet is currently a research preview for U.S. Claude Pro and Max subscribers, with plans starting at $20 per month. There's no separate Duet subscription fee during the preview, but its background activity shares the same usage limits as regular Claude.

And the deeper you look, the more interesting the trade-offs become.

Anthropic advertises more than 6,000 connectors and plugins, but that number hasn't been independently verified. Duet names integrations including Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Slack, Shopify, Stripe, QuickBooks, HubSpot, DocuSign, Canva, and Gusto. Yet some integrations have restrictions, and others aren't available at all.

We break down what Claude Duet can actually access, why its proactive monitoring isn't truly real-time, and how its cloud computer handles complex workflows without requiring your phone or laptop to stay online.

Anthropic's demonstrations show Duet building business dashboards, preparing investor meetings, tracking customer churn, managing invoices, and coordinating work across multiple business systems. One example, Marlo Pulse, combines information from sales, payroll, customer support, banking, and CRM tools.

But these are Anthropic's demonstrations—not independently verified reliability benchmarks.

Then there's one of Duet's most consequential capabilities: spending money.

Through Link by Stripe and Shop Pay, Duet can find products, request your approval, and complete purchases using merchant-specific, amount-limited virtual cards. It must pause before payments, messages, signatures, and deletions. Securities trading and account-to-account money transfers remain prohibited.

So how autonomous is this agent really?

We also examine early independent testing from Dan Shipper at Every and Claire Vo. Their experiences reveal promising interfaces and useful automation, alongside slow responses, limited proactive nudges, weaker email drafts, connector restrictions, and missing desktop functionality.

Security raises another important question. Duet processes emails, websites, and other third-party content, making prompt injection a genuine concern. Anthropic describes safeguards for credentials, sensitive information, and high-risk actions, but hasn't published Duet-specific reliability or security failure rates.

Finally, we compare Claude Duet with competing AI agents from OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, and Meta. From webhook-triggered automation and local computer control to persistent cloud execution and pricing, each takes a different approach to building an AI assistant that works without constant prompting.

The central question isn't whether Claude Duet can perform impressive tasks. Anthropic has demonstrated that it can.

It's whether Duet can consistently recognize what matters, make the right decisions, and complete real work reliably when nobody is watching.

That's the part nobody has independently measured yet.

videos.title: Sam Altman and Jony Ive’s Secret OpenAI Device Could Change Everything
videos.summary_source_text:
Sam Altman and Jony Ive’s Secret OpenAI Device Could Change Everything OpenAI reportedly spent $6.5 BILLION to bring Jony Ive's hardware startup into the company. Now leaks point to a battery-powered, doughnut-shaped AI device with a camera, no screen, and potentially moving parts. But the bigger story? OpenAI and Apple are locked in a federal court battle over alleged stolen hardware secrets, and both sides are accusing the other of mishandling confidential information.

Sam Altman and legendary iPhone designer Jony Ive want to build an entirely new category of AI hardware. Not another smartphone. Not another Alexa. Something designed around artificial intelligence from the beginning.

But can OpenAI actually succeed where Humane's AI Pin and Rabbit R1 struggled?

In May 2025, OpenAI announced its acquisition of io Products in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $6.5 billion. The startup, co-founded by Jony Ive and former Apple engineers, brought around 55 employees into OpenAI. Reports also suggest OpenAI has recruited more than 400 people from Apple as it builds a serious consumer hardware operation.

And the leaked device sounds unlike anything OpenAI has released before.

Imagine an AI companion that understands what's happening around you, remembers useful context, and potentially helps manage everyday tasks without constantly opening an app.

But there's an important distinction: OpenAI has NOT officially confirmed these specifications.

Greg Brockman has confirmed that OpenAI is developing a family of devices, describing an ambient, low-friction experience. However, the exact design, capabilities, and whether the first device will even be screenless remain uncertain.

Then there's the Apple lawsuit.

In July 2026, Apple sued OpenAI and former employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu, alleging the misuse of confidential hardware information. Apple claims sensitive engineering files, product designs, and supplier information were improperly accessed or transferred.

OpenAI denies those allegations.

And on October 14, the dispute took another turn. OpenAI alleged that a former employee transferred more than 100 confidential files related to an unreleased OpenAI device and later presented information to Apple leadership.

Apple disputes that account, saying it has found no supporting evidence.

Neither side's allegations have been proven in court.

This legal battle matters because Apple and OpenAI are simultaneously partners through ChatGPT's integration with Apple Intelligence and potential competitors in the next generation of AI hardware.

But even without the lawsuit, OpenAI faces enormous challenges.

Always-on cameras raise serious privacy questions. Cloud-based AI introduces latency and reliability concerns. Battery life becomes difficult when microphones, sensors, speakers, and potentially motors operate inside a compact device.

And then there's the price.

One unconfirmed report suggests a possible $300–$400 price range. That's a difficult proposition when Amazon Echo devices cost considerably less and smartphones already provide access to powerful AI assistants.

Humane's $699 AI Pin failed to establish a compelling alternative to the smartphone. Rabbit R1 faced similar criticism. Meanwhile, Meta's AI smart glasses demonstrate that consumers may embrace AI hardware when it fits naturally into their lives.

So what makes OpenAI's approach different?

We examine the reported hardware, the potential role of AI memory and environmental awareness, the growing competition with Apple and Google, and why Jony Ive's design philosophy could be central to the entire strategy.

We also break down the uncertain launch timeline. Despite earlier reports pointing toward late 2026, OpenAI has revealed no official product name, confirmed price, or public demonstration. A 2027 arrival may be more realistic, but that remains speculation.

The biggest question isn't whether OpenAI can build an intelligent speaker.

It's whether Sam Altman and Jony Ive can create an AI device useful enough to justify owning something separate from your phone.

And with Apple's lawsuit potentially exposing previously confidential hardware details, the next major revelation might come from a courtroom rather than a product announcement.

#OpenAI #JonyIve #SamAltman #AIHardware #Apple OpenAI reportedly spent $6.5 BILLION to bring Jony Ive's hardware startup into the company. Now leaks point to a battery-powered, doughnut-shaped AI device with a camera, no screen, and potentially moving parts. But the bigger story? OpenAI and Apple are locked in a federal court battle over alleged stolen hardware secrets, and both sides are accusing the other of mishandling confidential information.

Sam Altman and legendary iPhone designer Jony Ive want to build an entirely new category of AI hardware. Not another smartphone. Not another Alexa. Something designed around artificial intelligence from the beginning.

But can OpenAI actually succeed where Humane's AI Pin and Rabbit R1 struggled?

In May 2025, OpenAI announced its acquisition of io Products in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $6.5 billion. The startup, co-founded by Jony Ive and former Apple engineers, brought around 55 employees into OpenAI. Reports also suggest OpenAI has recruited more than 400 people from Apple as it builds a serious consumer hardware operation.

And the leaked device sounds unlike anything OpenAI has released before.

Imagine an AI companion that understands what's happening around you, remembers useful context, and potentially helps manage everyday tasks without constantly opening an app.

But there's an important distinction: OpenAI has NOT officially confirmed these specifications.

Greg Brockman has confirmed that OpenAI is developing a family of devices, describing an ambient, low-friction experience. However, the exact design, capabilities, and whether the first device will even be screenless remain uncertain.

Then there's the Apple lawsuit.

In July 2026, Apple sued OpenAI and former employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu, alleging the misuse of confidential hardware information. Apple claims sensitive engineering files, product designs, and supplier information were improperly accessed or transferred.

OpenAI denies those allegations.

And on October 14, the dispute took another turn. OpenAI alleged that a former employee transferred more than 100 confidential files related to an unreleased OpenAI device and later presented information to Apple leadership.

Apple disputes that account, saying it has found no supporting evidence.

Neither side's allegations have been proven in court.

This legal battle matters because Apple and OpenAI are simultaneously partners through ChatGPT's integration with Apple Intelligence and potential competitors in the next generation of AI hardware.

But even without the lawsuit, OpenAI faces enormous challenges.

Always-on cameras raise serious privacy questions. Cloud-based AI introduces latency and reliability concerns. Battery life becomes difficult when microphones, sensors, speakers, and potentially motors operate inside a compact device.

And then there's the price.

One unconfirmed report suggests a possible $300–$400 price range. That's a difficult proposition when Amazon Echo devices cost considerably less and smartphones already provide access to powerful AI assistants.

Humane's $699 AI Pin failed to establish a compelling alternative to the smartphone. Rabbit R1 faced similar criticism. Meanwhile, Meta's AI smart glasses demonstrate that consumers may embrace AI hardware when it fits naturally into their lives.

So what makes OpenAI's approach different?

We examine the reported hardware, the potential role of AI memory and environmental awareness, the growing competition with Apple and Google, and why Jony Ive's design philosophy could be central to the entire strategy.

We also break down the uncertain launch timeline. Despite earlier reports pointing toward late 2026, OpenAI has revealed no official product name, confirmed price, or public demonstration. A 2027 arrival may be more realistic, but that remains speculation.

The biggest question isn't whether OpenAI can build an intelligent speaker.

It's whether Sam Altman and Jony Ive can create an AI device useful enough to justify owning something separate from your phone.

And with Apple's lawsuit potentially exposing previously confidential hardware details, the next major revelation might come from a courtroom rather than a product announcement.

When You Understand This, The Golf Swing Becomes Effortless Struggle with inconsistent ball striking, coming over the top or feeling like your golf swing takes too much effort?

In this Danny Maude golf lesson, you’ll learn how the right arm should move in the golf swing to help you strike your irons more consistently, hit driver straighter and create a smoother, more effortless golf swing.

A lot of golfers make the swing much harder than it needs to be because the right shoulder and right arm get blocked very early in the backswing. When that happens, the elbow can move behind the body, the club becomes difficult to control and you may be forced to compensate on the way down.

In this lesson, Danny Maude shows you a much simpler way to organise the right arm so the golf club can move back freely and then be thrown naturally underneath through impact.

In this golf lesson you’ll learn:

• How the right arm should move in the golf swing  
• Why the right shoulder can block your backswing  
• How to create more space for the trail arm at setup  
• Why the shoulder blade should move naturally in the backswing  
• How an underarm throwing action can improve your downswing  
• How to stop coming over the top  
• A simple drill for golfers who pull or slice the ball  
• How to improve iron strike without forcing shaft lean  
• Why body position affects whether you hit ball then turf  
• How to create a more effortless and powerful golf swing  

The key is to picture the golf swing more like **bowling a ball underarm down an alleyway**.

Instead of forcing the club into positions, allow the right arm to move freely around you and then throw the club underneath towards the target. When the arm has enough space to move, the body can begin to organise itself much more naturally around the task.

There’s a lot of confusion surrounding peptides. A peptide is a short chain of amino acids that acts as a signal, telling the body to perform specific tasks, including building tendons, collagen, muscles, and ligaments.

GLP-1 is produced naturally in the gut and signals the body that you’re no longer hungry. This signal normally fades quickly, but certain GLP-1 weight loss drugs can remain active for up to seven days. This leads to decreased appetite and weight loss but can also cause gastrointestinal problems, muscle loss, and other side effects.

BPC-157 peptide injections have shown promising results for reducing knee pain, although human research remains limited.

Are peptides safe? Peptide safety largely depends on their source and quality. Much of the raw material used to manufacture peptides originates in China, and testing of some products has revealed incorrect amino acid sequences. Some products may also contain bacterial endotoxins, raising additional safety concerns.

Round 3 Highlights | 2026 Genesis Championship Round three highlights of the 2026 Genesis Championship. Highlights include Casey Jarvis, Ryan Fox, Si Woo Kim and Yuto Katsuragawa.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 38 events, the immediate future for some players on the DP World Tour depends on their performance at this week's Genesis Championship, the final event of the regular season brings drama aplenty and for the third year running South Korea is the base for it to unfold. Following on from Byeong Hun An's success two years ago, it was Junghwan Lee who triumphed 12 months ago as he became a DP World Tour winner for the first time. There are 39 players from South Korea teeing it up, headlined by recent Presidents Cup teammates Si Woo Kim and Sungjae Im as they look add DP World Tour glory to their CVs. Eugenio Chacarra will aim to bolster his lead at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World, following a run of form that has seen him finish third, second and then first last week in India across his last three starts. He is one of 11 winners from this season on the DP World Tour teeing up, with fellow multiple winner Casey Jarvis and Open champion Ryan Fox among them. The leading 70 available players in the Rankings at the end of this week will play their way into the field for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship next month. It’s time for an incredible Ferrari V12 showdown!

We’ve got our hands on a 12Cilindri Spider, an 812 GTS, an F12, and a 599 GTB, and they’re about to go head-to-head over the quarter mile!

The question is, will the more recent releases leave the others in their wake? Or could the F12 or 599 spring a surprise on the others? Let’s take a closer look at the stats…

Starting with the 599 GTB, it’s powered by a 6-litre NA V12 that delivers 620hp and 608Nm. It’s the only car here without a dual-clutch gearbox, and it weighs in at 1,690kg. When new way back in 2006, it cost around £172,000.

Next up is the F12 Berlinetta. It’s equipped with a 6.3-litre NA V12, and this delivers 740hp and 690Nm. Power is sent to the rear wheels only via a 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox, and it’s the lightest car here, weighing in at 1,630kg. Back in 2012, it cost around £240,000.

Following this, we have the 812 GTS. It’s powered by a 6.5-litre NA V12, and this creates 800hp and 718Nm. Power’s sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed dual-clutch, and it weighs in at 1,700kg. When new in 2019, it cost around £293,000.

Finally, we come to the 12Cilindri. Like the 812 GTS, it has a 6.5-litre NA V12, and this puts down 830hp and 678Nm. This is sent to the rears by an 8-speed dual-clutch, and it’s the heaviest car here, weighing in at around 1,720kg. In 2024, it cost around £366,000.

So will the newer 812 & 12Cilindri walk it? There’s only one way to find out for sure… LET’S RACE!

videos.summary_source_text:
23.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Avalanche Move On From the Bad Road Trip, Take Down Tampa Colorado Avalanche silence the Tampa Bay Lightning with Nathan MacKinnon’s explosive four-point night. Is this the start of another dominant run for the Avs?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down Colorado’s 6-3 victory, spotlighting MacKinnon’s highlight-reel speed, Artturi Lehkonen’s clutch nine-goal season tally, and Logan O’Connor’s game-changing penalty kill return. The conversation focused on pivotal moments including smart power play adjustments, the impact of Mackenzie Blackwood’s stellar goaltending, and controversial penalty calls involving Nikita Kucherov and Andrei Vasilevskiy. Key themes include the Avalanche’s improved resilience, the pressure release of early goals, and critical contributions from rising talents like TJ Hughes. Can Colorado sustain this momentum and tighten up defensively to stay atop the Western Conference?

Don’t miss the insight into Jared Bednar’s evolving strategies and what lies ahead as the Avs chase another shot at the Stanley Cup.

videos.title: Still slicing your driver? Please check this...
videos.summary_source_text:
Still slicing your driver? Please check this... Still slicing your driver? Check your right elbow 👀

https://sbrew.link/rIqYTvzs

Save this golf drill for your next practice session and send it to a golfer who’s tired of missing right!

If the tip of your right elbow never gets in front of your shirt seam during the downswing, your hips and shoulders may spin open sending the club across the ball and straight into “sliced city.” 🏌️‍♂️➡️

Try this instead: let your arms drop, tuck your right elbow just in front of your shirt seam, and allow the club to shallow behind you. This helps you approach the ball from the inside so you can hit straighter drives, create a draw, and find more fairways.

The Blue Brick makes this drill even more effective by giving you instant feedback when you spin out or come over the top.

Ready to fix your slice and build a more consistent driver swing?

videos.title: Elon Musk's MACROHARD: The AI Company With Zero Employees
videos.summary_source_text:
Elon Musk's MACROHARD: The AI Company With Zero Employees Elon Musk claims his AI project, Macrohard, could eventually simulate an entire software company like Microsoft. Now he's saying its Digital Optimus system can play halfway through Diablo using only computer vision. But there's a problem: no public demonstration, no independent benchmark, and no verified success rate.

Meanwhile, one of the toughest independent AI computer-use benchmarks, OSWorld 2.0, found that its best tested configuration completed just **20.6% of 108 complex workflows**. So how close are we really to AI agents that can operate computers, perform human jobs, and potentially run entire businesses?

The story starts in October 2021, when Musk joked that "Macrohard" was better than Microsoft. By August 2025, xAI had filed a trademark application and Musk was describing a purely AI software company powered by Grok and hundreds of specialized agents.

But the project didn't stay the same.

By February 2026, Musk was describing something much more ambitious: "digital human emulation." Instead of simply building software, Macrohard would aim to perform virtually any task a human can accomplish on a computer, from customer support and legacy enterprise applications to CAD and chip design.

Then came the major Tesla pivot.

On March 11, Musk announced that Macrohard, also called Digital Optimus, had become a joint Tesla and xAI project. The proposed architecture combines Grok as a high-level planner with a Tesla-built computer-control agent that processes approximately five seconds of live screen video and recent keyboard and mouse activity.

Musk says the low-level system runs on Tesla's AI4 hardware while Grok operates on Nvidia-based servers. Unlike traditional screenshot-based computer agents, the goal is continuous, real-time interaction with software.

But reporting from Business Insider suggested the original xAI effort had stalled, with a computer-use data collection program involving more than 600 contractors reportedly paused.

And Tesla's own corporate documents tell a more restrained story.

Then there's Grok Bot.

Launched in public beta in August 2026, Grok Bot offers always-on AI agents with cloud computers, persistent context, multi-agent collaboration, and business workflow automation. Yet Musk explicitly distinguished it from Digital Optimus, describing the latter as real-time video-based human emulation.

That distinction matters when evaluating what Tesla and xAI have actually demonstrated.

On October 10, Musk claimed Digital Optimus could progress roughly halfway through Diablo, had developed Counter-Strike skills, and was training on League of Legends.

Those claims could be significant for real-time AI control. But without public gameplay footage, independent testing, intervention counts, or completion statistics, the actual capabilities remain unverified.

And the broader AI agent industry faces the same fundamental challenge: reliability.

OSWorld 2.0 reported a 20.6% completion rate for its strongest tested Claude Opus 4.8 configuration under its main 500-step limit. TheAgentCompany, another benchmark simulating software-company tasks, reported a 24% autonomous completion rate for its strongest baseline at publication.

These are historical benchmark results, not definitive measurements of today's newest AI systems. But they expose a critical problem: performing individual actions is very different from reliably completing long, complicated workflows.

Even a hypothetical agent that's 99.9% accurate per action has only about a 60.6% chance of completing 500 independent actions without an error.

So what happens when AI agents must handle confidential company information, unpredictable software, security threats, changing instructions, and decisions that can't be verified with simple tests?

We examine how Macrohard compares with OpenAI Dots, Anthropic's computer-use systems and Cowork, Google's Gemini computer-use capabilities, Microsoft, Amazon, and Manus.

Macrohard is more than a joke. Tesla's roadmap, engineering recruitment, and proposed architecture point to a real development effort. But whether its real-time computer-control approach can outperform competing AI agents remains an open question.

Could Musk's Digital Optimus become the foundation of an AI-powered Microsoft? Or is the gap between impressive demonstrations and reliable autonomous businesses much larger than the headlines suggest?

videos.title: Claude Mythos 5 Just Made a Massive Quantum Computing Breakthrough
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Mythos 5 Just Made a Massive Quantum Computing Breakthrough Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 reportedly cut a quantum circuit's gate count by nearly 12 times. Jack Clark now thinks fully self-improving AI could arrive in 2027. The FTC is demanding internal safety records from OpenAI and Anthropic. And Google's Gemini 4 Argon is going head-to-head with GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5.

But behind these headlines are some important details that change the story.

Claude Mythos 5 reportedly reduced a Reed-Solomon quantum decoder from roughly 5.1 million Toffoli gates to just 440,000, using a different algorithm rather than simply optimizing the original design. There's a catch: these circuits were tested in simulation, not on actual quantum hardware. The research is a preprint, independent replication is still missing, and the supposedly autonomous process involved human guidance. So is this an AI scientific breakthrough, or a narrower achievement being stretched into a bigger narrative?

That question becomes more interesting when Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark moves his forecast for full recursive self-improvement (RSI) from 2028 to 2027. He points to progress in AI creativity and research judgment, including TasteVal results suggesting AI research taste has been doubling approximately every three months. But a benchmark trend is not proof that AI can autonomously build its own successor.

Meanwhile, AI safety is becoming a regulatory issue.

The Federal Trade Commission has reportedly issued civil investigative demands exceeding 50 pages to OpenAI and Anthropic, seeking documents involving security incidents, safeguards, privacy policies, and marketing claims. These demands are not findings of wrongdoing, but they could expose differences between public AI safety promises and internal testing.

Anthropic is also taking an unusual approach to external oversight. Six researchers from METR have been granted employee-like access to evaluate frontier AI systems, with Anthropic promising not to veto their published conclusions. Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/1hXpb3T96PU

Potassium works with sodium to power the pumps in your cells that generate electrical impulses and regulate fluid balance. 

When potassium is low, you might experience:
• Fatigue and low energy
• Muscle cramps
• Heart palpitations
• High blood pressure
• Fluid retention

Avocados and leafy greens are excellent sources of potassium, but many people struggle to get enough through their diet. A high-potassium electrolyte supplement can help increase your intake and support a healthy electrolyte balance.

videos.title: Round 2 Highlights | 2026 Genesis Championship
videos.summary_source_text:
Round 2 Highlights | 2026 Genesis Championship Highlights of the 2026 Genesis Championship. Highlights include Casey Jarvis, Ryan Fox and Eugenio Chacarra. 

After 38 events, the immediate future for some players on the DP World Tour depends on their performance at this week's Genesis Championship, the final event of the regular season brings drama aplenty and for the third year running South Korea is the base for it to unfold. Following on from Byeong Hun An's success two years ago, it was Junghwan Lee who triumphed 12 months ago as he became a DP World Tour winner for the first time. There are 39 players from South Korea teeing it up, headlined by recent Presidents Cup teammates Si Woo Kim and Sungjae Im as they look add DP World Tour glory to their CVs. Eugenio Chacarra will aim to bolster his lead at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World, following a run of form that has seen him finish third, second and then first last week in India across his last three starts. He is one of 11 winners from this season on the DP World Tour teeing up, with fellow multiple winner Casey Jarvis and Open champion Ryan Fox among them. The leading 70 available players in the Rankings at the end of this week will play their way into the field for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship next month. The top 50 after that will earn a place at the DP World Tour Championship, the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events.
